run.question: Which service has the most error events in the events collection? What is the most common error code for that service and how many times does it appear?

report.summary: The MongoDB database opsdb contains a single collection, events (200 documents per the collection's estimated count, and the aggregation over the 200 documents read returned a total of 200). Grouping all documents by service and level shows payment-processor holds the most error-level events: 47, ahead of inventory-sync (31), user-auth (25), notification-hub (18) and search-indexer (12); the five error counts sum to 133, which matches the collection-wide error-level total of 133 (versus 67 info), so no error-level group is unaccounted for. For payment-processor, grouping its 47 error-level events by the error_code field shows TXN-4821 is the most common value with 23 occurrences, followed by TXN-5190 with 14 and TXN-3007 with 10 (23+14+10 = 47). The error_code values have the shape of transaction identifiers (e.g. TXN-4821) rather than numeric status codes; the field is reported exactly as the collection schema names it. Caveat: every document's timestamp lies in 2025-12-01T00:00:00 to 2025-12-01T03:19:00, which is before the authorized window (2026-10-24T18:49:05Z to 2026-11-23T18:49:05Z), so these counts describe the collection as read at query time and cannot be scoped to, or attributed to, the authorized incident window. No fault or causal object was established, so no root cause is named.

claims.text: The opsdb database contains exactly one collection, named events, of type collection.
The events collection documents carry the fields _id, error_code, level, message, service and timestamp, with an estimated document count of 200.

Grouping events by service and level returns 10 groups: level=error counts of payment-processor 47, inventory-sync 31, user-auth 25, notification-hub 18, search-indexer 12, and level=info counts of inventory-sync 14, payment-processor 14, search-indexer 13, user-auth 13, notification-hub 13; no further service/level group exists in the collection.
The collection-wide totals are level=error 133 and level=info 67, i.e. 200 documents, so the five error-level service counts (47+31+25+18+12=133) account for every error-level event.

For payment-processor error-level events, grouping by error_code gives TXN-4821 = 23, TXN-5190 = 14, TXN-3007 = 10, so TXN-4821 is the most common error_code value with 23 occurrences out of 47 payment-processor error events.

Payment-processor error documents pair those codes with distinct messages: TXN-4821 'Transaction timeout waiting for bank response' (23), TXN-5190 'Currency conversion service unavailable' (14), TXN-3007 'Duplicate transaction ID detected' (10); its 14 info documents are spread over seven message types with 2 each.

Sample payment-processor error documents show error_code values that look like transaction identifiers (TXN-4821) alongside message 'Transaction timeout waiting for bank response' and timestamps of 2025-12-01T00:00:00 onwards.
Across the whole collection the timestamp range is 2025-12-01T00:00:00 to 2025-12-01T03:19:00 over 200 documents, i.e. every event lies before the authorized window start of 2026-10-24T18:49:05Z.

The event_data target's service naming does not match the trace-side service list: payment-processor, inventory-sync, user-auth, notification-hub and search-indexer are MongoDB event services, while the registered trace services are accounting, ad, cart, checkout, currency, email, fraud-detection, frontend, frontend-proxy, image-provider, kafka, load-generator, payment, product-catalog, quote, recommendation and shipping; the two cannot be equated without further evidence.

The error_code field holds transaction-level identifiers rather than HTTP/gRPC status codes, so 'TXN-4821' most likely identifies a failing or repeated transaction (its message is 'Transaction timeout waiting for bank response') rather than an error class; this is not confirmed by any schema description or code evidence.

gaps: All 200 event documents are timestamped 2025-12-01T00:00:00 to 2025-12-01T03:19:00, before the authorized window, so the counts cannot be presented as activity inside the incident window; the answer reflects the collection as read at query time (2026-11-23T18:49:05Z).

No schema description or documentation was available for the error_code field, so whether it is a transaction ID or an error class could not be verified; only the field name and observed values are known.

Events are read-only and unreadable fields or documents invisible to the read-only account cannot be ruled out; the 200-document total rests on the estimated document count and the aggregation count, both of which returned 200.

Correlation with the trace/metric sources for payment-processor was not checked, and the MongoDB event service names do not appear in the trace service list, so nothing is asserted about the health or error rate of any traced service.
next_steps: If the incident-window view matters, confirm with the collection owner why every event carries a 2025-12-01 timestamp and whether events are appended with a different clock or were backfilled.
Ask the schema owner whether error_code is a transaction identifier or an error classification before using it as an error-code taxonomy.
Optionally cross-check payment-processor behavior against the Prometheus payment service and the frontend/checkout traces before drawing any incident conclusion.
